approval_scope: offline evidence and exact non-executable Phase 8.9 blueprint; no claim of deployed or live-cloud verification

whole_profile_limitations: An all-GCP whole Twin remains unsupported until the separately owned L4/L5 capability gap is closed; the GCP embedded-event and Event-Layer scopes remain admissible.
All six directed workload-identity exchanges remain live activation gates rather than observed cloud evidence.
The GCP BifroMQ allocation is theoretically dimensioned but must pass the selected-version 64-KiB throughput, ordering, and failure gate before activation.

pricing_completeness_result.scope: incremental embedded domain-event, Event-Layer, bridge, landing, transfer, retention, workflow, device boundary, and observability costs; not full-profile totals

known_differences: six-layer-eventing@1 is validated as a standalone PoC architecture without inheritance from an intermediate runtime profile.
Provider bundles are functionally aligned compositions, not one-to-one service equivalents.

Single-cloud paths use the complete local event-domain bundle and no bridge; this does not claim a complete executable whole Twin. Cross-cloud paths use source-owned durable forwarding to the destination broker data plane.

EMQX Cloud Dedicated Flex is functionally admissible but not selected because its public reproducible price matrix stops below the 100,000-session Large scenario; cost was not used to choose the cheapest service.
The published cost results are separate event-scope estimates and intentionally do not rank full Twin profiles.

A pre-activation implementation review on 2026-08-08 replaced the planning-only unlimited operator wait for route faults with the already costed six-attempt provider budget, an application-safe terminal record where the trigger exposes the current attempt, and the selected provider-native terminal destination as fallback; functional scope and selected services did not change.

A pre-activation contract review on 2026-08-08 superseded the planning-only eventing-envelope.v1 with the shared canonical-domain-event.v1 used by both approved profiles and the runtime; ordering is source_id/source_sequence, consumer idempotency is event_id, and optional redrive identity is payload.replay_id. Selected services, workload sizes, and cost formulas did not change.

The standalone Phase 8.8 scenarios price the eight core event-domain channels. The closed bridge/runtime registry also permits the four twin_projection.v1 profile-extension variants whose explicit workloads and route costs are owned by the later complete-service profile calculation; this separation prevents projection traffic from being omitted at profile level or double-counted in the earlier event-scope figures.

residual_risks.gate: Execute and capture issuer, audience, subject, expiry, destination authorization, and negative-claim tests for all six directed provider pairs; for AWS-to-Azure also prove account-level outbound federation enablement and use of a regional rather than global STS endpoint.
residual_risks.consequence: A failing direction is unsupported and must block any profile placement that requires it.

residual_risks.gate: Run supervised throughput, backlog, retry, ordering, and failure tests for AWS 400-shard Kinesis, Azure six-CU Dedicated Event Hubs, GCP 126 event-delivery workers, and the GCP 12-broker-plus-four-integration-node BifroMQ boundary with 300 ordered shared clients.
residual_risks.consequence: Theoretical capacity is not sufficient to activate a Large deployment.

residual_risks.gate: Pin the reviewed image digest and chart; implement the explicit ordered MQTT-to-Pub/Sub adapter, reconnect ordering-degradation evidence, mTLS/authorization, scenario topology, three inbox replicas, backup, upgrade, and cleanup ownership in Phase 8.9.
residual_risks.consequence: The full bidirectional GCP device boundary is acceptable for this PoC but is neither managed nor production-qualified and cannot activate before its live capacity and failure test passes.

residual_risks.gate: Keep all-GCP whole-profile resolution fail-closed until the separately owned L4/L5 capability gap has an approved implementation.
residual_risks.consequence: GCP Eventing evidence must not be misreported as an executable all-GCP Twin.

evidence: The historical @1 boundary, both event-enabled target profiles, and rejection of all three legacy flags were inspected.
Nine embedded and fifteen Event-Layer capabilities, 37 service components, ten adapters, eight logical edges, and six route classes with two exact profile bindings each were reconciled.
Every source outbox owns its provider bridge adapter; the three bridge runtimes are shared in 8.9A while route endpoints and cost ownership remain profile-specific.
The full bidirectional GCP BifroMQ/GKE boundary, ordered MQTT-to-Pub/Sub adapter, scenario topology, reconnect degradation, and live capacity/failure gate were checked.
All six directed trust paths use short-lived credentials; AWS-to-Azure additionally requires account-enabled outbound federation and a regional STS endpoint.
All 66 frozen primary sources and every formula, price, capability, source, and artifact reference passed strict offline verification.
Small, Medium, and Large results reproduce byte-identically for all three single-cloud event-domain cases, six directed pairs, and six three-provider placements.

Thirty focused calculator and package-validator tests pass, including negative formula, digest, capacity, route, profile-binding, source-adapter, identity-preflight, ownership, contract, and secret cases.
Cost is a visible outcome rather than the service-bundle selection criterion; Phase 8.8 is explicitly event-scope evidence and whole-Twin ranking remains Phase 8.10.
The Phase 8 roadmap, handoff, 8.8 gate, 8.9 implementation slices, 8.10 evaluation boundary, research note, and evidence README were checked for contradictory ownership or status claims.
